*.input.label-repeats-key: The receiver's own input words (AUDIO1, HDMI1, NET RADIO): the value is what the device calls the input and what a write sends; the label is the name the user gave it where the device reports one.
*.input.label-language: Input names are the device's texts — the names the user gave in the MusicCast app, or the receiver's own input words — in the language the device was set up in, not the adapter's.

*.multiroom.*.input.label-repeats-key: The same input words once per zone: the value is what the device calls the input and what a write sends.
*.multiroom.*.input.label-language: The same device-given input names once per zone, in the language the device was set up in.

*.soundProgram.label-repeats-key: Yamaha's DSP program names (Hall in Munich, The Roxy Theatre, 7ch Stereo) are the receiver's own words — the value it reports and a write sends; they are proper names, the same in every manual.
*.soundProgram.label-language: The program names a MusicCast device reports for its own list (getNameText), in the language the device chooses.

*.sound.surroundDecoder.label-repeats-key: The decoders are trademarks (Dolby Surround, DTS Neural:X, DTS NEO:6) and the receiver's own words; the automatic choice carries a label of its own.

*.advanced.speakers.pattern1Amp.label-repeats-key: The receiver's own amp-assignment names (Basic, 7.1 +1ZONE, …) exactly as its setup menu and manual show them.

*.scene.recall.label-language: Scene titles are the names the device carries for its scenes (BD/DVD, TV, NET, RADIO, or what the user renamed them to).

*.player.browse.rows.encoded-value: The menu window for visualisations, next to its eight single line datapoints (line1 to line8) that a script reads.

*.scene.list.encoded-value: The scene list for visualisations, next to the single title datapoints and the recall dropdown labelled with the same titles.

*.multiroom.*.scene.list.encoded-value: The zone's scene list for visualisations, next to its single title datapoints and its recall dropdown.

*.multiroom.group.linkedDevices.encoded-value: The group's client list for visualisations, next to one clients.<n>.ip datapoint per linked device.

*.player.netPlayer.playlists.encoded-value: The playlist list for visualisations, next to one playlistNames.<n>.name datapoint per playlist.

*.player.netPlayer.presets.encoded-value: The favourites list for visualisations, next to one favourites.<n> channel with name and source per slot.

*.player.netPlayer.recent.encoded-value: The recently played list for visualisations, next to one recentItems.<n> channel with name and source per entry.

*.player.netPlayer.queue.encoded-value: The play queue for visualisations, next to queueLength, queuePosition and one queueTracks.<n>.name datapoint per track.

*.tuner.presets.encoded-value: The stored stations per band for visualisations, next to one storedStations channel per stored station (per band where the device keeps a list per band).

$sameInEveryLanguage.USB: The connector's name, written the same in every language.
$sameInEveryLanguage.HDMI: The connector standard's name, written the same in every language.
$sameInEveryLanguage.Analog: German, Dutch and Polish-speaking manuals write the analog input the same way as English.
$sameInEveryLanguage.iPod (USB): A product name and a connector, written the same in every language.
$sameInEveryLanguage.Mono: The audio term is written the same in German as in English.
$sameInEveryLanguage.Stereo: The audio term is written the same in German as in English.
$sameInEveryLanguage.Zone 2: German writes a receiver zone the same way as English.
$sameInEveryLanguage.Zone 3: German writes a receiver zone the same way as English.
$sameInEveryLanguage.Zone 4: German writes a receiver zone the same way as English.
